SQL:
SELECT
  customers__cities.size_class AS "orders.customers.cities.size_class",
  CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.amount_sum",
  COUNT(*) AS "orders._count"
FROM orders AS orders
LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
  ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
LEFT JOIN cities AS customers__cities
  ON customers.city = customers__cities.city
  AND customers.region_id = customers__cities.region_id
GROUP BY
  customers__cities.size_class
LIMIT 21

args.message: Large-city customers bring in the most revenue: 205,080.28, from 3,110 orders. Medium is next at 100,075.84 (1,481 orders), then small at 26,339.03 (409 orders). The null group, 1,193.30 from 16 orders, is for orders whose customer's city has no match in the city reference table. Each order is matched to its customer, and the customer is matched to the city table on both city and region. Revenue is the sum of order amounts.
